subject: Overlay two distributions (but with different bin structure)

messages.author: e7a71d967e60bb41
messages.subject: Overlay two distributions (but with different bin structure)
parts:
Dear All,
Consider the snippet at the end of the email.
It bins two distributions and prints them on the same plot, allowing for
an overlap.
Now, I wonder if I can generate a similar plot, but specifying two
different bin widths (let us say 0.1 and 0.2) for the two distributions.
Any idea about how to achieve that?
Cheers

Lorenzo

######################################################
require(ggplot2)
x <- data.frame(value=rnorm(5000, mean=0), case="A")
y <- data.frame(value=rnorm(5000, mean=3), case="B")
xy <- rbind(x, y)
gpl <- ggplot(xy, aes(x=value, fill=case, group=case)) +
geom_histogram(alpha=0.5,binwidth=0.1, position="identity")

pdf("histogram_overlay.pdf")
print(gpl)
dev.off()

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: Overlay two distributions (but with different bin structure)
parts:
ggplot(subset(xy, case == "A"), aes(x=value, fill=case, group=case)) +
geom_histogram(alpha=0.5,binwidth=0.1, position="identity") +
geom_histogram(data = subset(xy, case == "B"),
alpha=0.5,binwidth=0.2, position="identity")

messages.subject: Re: Overlay two distributions (but with different bin structure)
parts:
Just thought I would add that it may make the graph easier to
interpret if you map density instead of count to the y axis:

gpl <- ggplot(subset(xy, case == "A"), aes(x=value, y = ..density..,

fill=case, group=case)) +
geom_histogram(alpha=0.5,binwidth=0.1, position="identity") +
geom_histogram(data = subset(xy, case == "B"),
alpha=0.5,binwidth=0.2, position="identity")
